_readme: DATA, not code. `core/intake/*.py` must never branch on a domain name; it
reads this file and matches `tokens` against evidence the workspace itself
produced (discovered table names, column names, document filenames, KPI
registry terms). A domain with no token match is never proposed.
`question_overlay` retunes an EXISTING intake question for a CONFIRMED
domain. Option ids are never introduced or renamed here -- only labels,
recommendations and suggested answers -- because core/blueprint/decisions.py

healthcare.label: Healthcare -- clinical, provider or payer operations

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: Direct identifiers (name, date of birth, address, contact, member/record number) plus anything that ties a person to a clinical event; only the care and billing teams may see them unmasked, analysts get masked or aggregated values.
pii_regulated.why: Health data is regulated by default, so the safe starting point names identifiers rather than waiting for someone to spot one.

lineage_reproducibility.why: A regulated number that cannot be reproduced as of its publication date cannot be defended in an audit, so this domain pays the cheaper-than-a-finding cost up front.

calendar_and_restatement.why: Late adjustments and corrections arrive after publication in this domain, so an append-only assumption silently understates already-published periods.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (adjustments, denials and corrections land after publication)

consumers.why: Compliance reporting is the consumer that can veto a design here; satisfying it first means the others get a lawful surface for free.

finance_banking.label: Finance / banking -- accounting, lending or capital markets

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: Account and card numbers, national identifiers, names and addresses on parties to a transaction; unmasked access limited to the finance and fraud teams, everyone else sees tokenised or aggregated values.
pii_regulated.why: The identifiers here are also payment credentials, so masking is the starting point rather than the exception.

lineage_reproducibility.why: A published financial figure has to be reproducible as of its reporting date, which is exactly what attribute-level lineage buys.

calendar_and_restatement.why: A closed accounting period is frozen and corrections go to the next period, so rebuilding history freely would contradict what was already reported.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (adjusting entries land before the period is closed)

consumers.why: The reporting pack with the hardest constraints wins; a surface that satisfies it also serves the internal readers.

insurance.label: Insurance -- underwriting, policy or claims operations

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: Policyholder and claimant identity (name, date of birth, address, national id), plus any health or loss detail attached to a claim; unmasked only for claims handling, masked for analysis.
pii_regulated.why: Claim detail often carries health or criminal information, which is regulated well beyond ordinary customer data.

lineage_reproducibility.why: Reserves and loss ratios are restated as claims develop, so every published figure needs an as-of-date reproduction.

calendar_and_restatement.why: Claims develop for months after the event, so published triangles are restated by design rather than appended to.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (claims develop for months after the loss date)

consumers.why: Statutory reporting is the binding consumer; the actuarial and operational readers sit on the same conformed layer.

retail_ecommerce.label: Retail / e-commerce -- orders, catalogue and fulfilment

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: Customer name, contact details, delivery address and payment reference; the marketing and analytics teams work from hashed customer keys, only fulfilment and support see contact details.
pii_regulated.why: Contact and delivery data is the disclosure risk here, and it is easy to keep out of the analytical surface entirely.

lineage_reproducibility.why: Trading numbers are re-derived from the current order book rather than defended as of a past date, so the cheaper default holds unless finance says otherwise.

calendar_and_restatement.why: Returns and cancellations land after the sale, so a day's revenue keeps moving for the length of the returns window.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (returns and cancellations land after the sale)

consumers.why: Trading review runs on a small set of known query shapes; more classes can be added once a second reader actually exists.

manufacturing_supply_chain.label: Manufacturing / supply chain -- production and procurement

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: Operator and approver names on work orders and inspections, plus supplier contact people; keep them out of the analytical layer and report by role or station instead.
pii_regulated.why: The personal data here is incidental to the process data, so it can usually be dropped rather than masked.

lineage_reproducibility.why: A quality escape has to be traced back to the lot and station that produced it, which is attribute-level lineage by another name.

calendar_and_restatement.why: Inspection and scrap outcomes are recorded after the production run, so the run's numbers are corrected after they are first published.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (inspection and scrap outcomes land after the run)

consumers.why: The number is acted on at the line rather than read in a pack, and an operational surface also feeds the reporting one.

telecom.label: Telecom -- network, subscriber and usage operations

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: Subscriber identifiers (MSISDN, IMSI, IMEI, account name) and anything that reveals location or who contacted whom; analysts get pseudonymised keys and coarse location only.
pii_regulated.why: Usage records are communications metadata, which is regulated separately from ordinary customer data in most jurisdictions.

lineage_reproducibility.why: A disputed bill has to be reconstructed from the usage as it was rated, not as the current rating rules would compute it.

calendar_and_restatement.why: Usage records arrive late from roaming partners and mediation, so an already-published day keeps growing for a known window.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (roaming and mediated usage records arrive late)

consumers.why: Network and commercial reviews share a fixed set of query shapes; widen only when a second class is named.

saas_product_analytics.label: SaaS / product analytics -- usage, funnel and subscription

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: End-user email, name, IP address and any free-text they typed; product analysis runs on hashed user and tenant ids, with raw identity limited to support.
pii_regulated.why: Behavioural events are personal data once they carry a stable user id, and the analytical use rarely needs the raw identity.

lineage_reproducibility.why: Product metrics are re-derived from the event log rather than defended as of a past date, so the cheaper default holds.

calendar_and_restatement.why: Late-arriving client events and session stitching change yesterday's counts for a day or two after publication.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (late client events and session stitching change yesterday)

consumers.why: The question set here is genuinely exploratory, and a conformed model is what keeps ad-hoc answers agreeing with each other.

hr_people.label: HR / people operations -- workforce, payroll and hiring

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: Everything that identifies a person plus pay, performance, health and disciplinary detail; access is restricted to HR, and every other reader sees values aggregated above a minimum group size.
pii_regulated.why: In this domain nearly the whole record is sensitive, and small groups re-identify people even when identifiers are removed.

lineage_reproducibility.why: Pay and headcount figures are challenged after the fact, so each has to be reproducible exactly as it was published.

calendar_and_restatement.why: Backdated hires, leavers and pay corrections change an already-reported period as a matter of routine.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (backdated hires, leavers and pay corrections)

consumers.why: Statutory pay and diversity reporting has the strictest constraints, and satisfying it makes the management view safe by construction.

logistics.label: Logistics -- freight, transport and last-mile delivery

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: Recipient name, address and contact number, plus driver identity and position traces; keep addresses at postcode level for analysis and leave full detail in the operational system.
pii_regulated.why: Delivery addresses and driver traces are both personal data, and analysis almost never needs either at full precision.

lineage_reproducibility.why: Service performance is recomputed from the current event history rather than defended as of a past date.

calendar_and_restatement.why: Scan events arrive out of order from partners, so a day's on-time rate settles only after the late scans land.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (scan events arrive out of order from partners)

consumers.why: The number drives a dispatch or exception decision while the shipment is moving, so the operational surface comes first.

energy_utilities.label: Energy / utilities -- metering, generation and grid

pii_regulated.suggested_answer: Metering point identifiers tied to a household, plus account name and address; half-hourly consumption reveals occupancy, so analysis runs on aggregated or pseudonymised meter keys.
pii_regulated.why: Interval consumption is personal data because it exposes when a home is occupied, which is easy to miss when the column looks purely numeric.

lineage_reproducibility.why: Settlement and billing figures are audited against the readings as they stood at settlement time.

calendar_and_restatement.why: Estimated readings are replaced by actuals through the settlement window, restating already-published consumption.

option_labels.restate_within_window: Published numbers are restated within a known window (estimated readings are replaced by actuals at settlement)

consumers.why: Settlement and regulatory submissions bind the design; internal reporting rides on the same conformed numbers.
